headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage from shared workspace content; prompt injection and cascading errors are limited by the pair's narrow surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can read workspace pages and databases, and the profile says shared workspace state exists across instances. spring-integration-samples has no documented ingestion path, so the interaction is inferred, but shared workspace content can carry attacker-controlled instructions that Notion AI may treat as trusted. The pairwise pathway is plausible without extra tooling, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples content is copied into a shared Notion page or database
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or act on that shared content without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate untrusted project notes from operational Notion pages
Add a visible provenance banner to imported content
Require manual review before acting on AI-generated instructions
Use a dedicated workspace for untrusted material
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging and filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while the other profile is a docs-only open-source sample with no data surfaces. The pair shares workspace state on the Notion side, so leakage is plausible if sensitive workspace content is placed into pages that the AI processes. The second agent does not add a documented exfiltration path, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are accessible to Notion AI
IF those pages are used as input for summaries, Q&A, or drafting
mitigations: Restrict sensitive pages from AI-accessible workspaces
Mark confidential databases as off-limits for AI use
Review AI outputs before sharing externally
Split public and sensitive content into separate workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce per-page AI access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification, and spring-integration-samples is not runnable and exposes no write capabilities. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration outside the profiles, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable workspace
IF spring-integration-samples is wrapped with additional write permissions not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep the sample repo read-only
Avoid mapping both agents to the same mutable directory
Document ownership of shared pages
Use separate service accounts
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI can generate workspace-grounded text, but spring-integration-samples is not runnable and has no documented downstream action authority. The pair therefore lacks a clear default chain where one agent's output is automatically executed by the other. Any cascade would require an external workflow that is not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external workflow feeds Notion AI output into an automated action step
IF spring-integration-samples is repurposed as an execution target outside the documented profile
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Do not auto-import AI text into executors
Label AI-generated content clearly
Use verification checklists for any copied instructions
requires-engineering: add output validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through Notion backends, while spring-integration-samples is an open-source sample with no data residency or retention profile. The only concrete compliance concern is that workspace content may be processed by Notion's vendor environment; the second agent is not a documented compliance sink, so this is a limited mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages accessible to AI
IF the organization requires on-prem or self-hosted processing only
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AI-enabled pages
Review vendor terms for retention and residency
Use a separate workspace for regulated content
Disable AI on compliance-sensitive databases
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
